claims.quote: A bulbous cell that is medially placed in one row in the organ of Corti.
The stereocilia from inner hair cells extend into small dimples on the tectorial membrane’s lower surface.

source.citation: Clark MA, Douglas M, Choi J (2018). Biology 2e. OpenStax.

claims.quote: The organs of Corti contain hair cells, which are named for the hair-like stereocilia extending from the cell’s apical surfaces

source.citation: Betts JG, Young KA, Wise JA, Johnson E, Poe B, Kruse DH, Korol O, Johnson JE, Womble M, DeSaix P (2022). Anatomy and Physiology 2e. OpenStax.

claims.value: stereocilia array graded in height from tallest to shortest
claims.quote: The stereocilia are an array of microvilli-like structures arranged from tallest to shortest.

source.citation: Betts JG, Young KA, Wise JA, Johnson E, Poe B, Kruse DH, Korol O, Johnson JE, Womble M, DeSaix P (2022). Anatomy and Physiology 2e. OpenStax.

claims.value: protein tethers linking adjacent stereocilia within each array
claims.quote: Protein fibers tether adjacent hairs together within each array, such that the array will bend in response to movements of the basilar membrane.

source.citation: Betts JG, Young KA, Wise JA, Johnson E, Poe B, Kruse DH, Korol O, Johnson JE, Womble M, DeSaix P (2022). Anatomy and Physiology 2e. OpenStax.

claims.value: fewer sensory hairs than outer hair cells
claims.quote: In contrast to the outer hair cells, the inner hair cells are fewer in number, have fewer sensory hairs, and are less differentiated.

claims.value: afferent synapses: each inner hair cell synapses with about 10 afferent neurons
claims.quote: About 90 percent of the afferent neurons carry information from inner hair cells, with each hair cell synapsing with 10 or so neurons.

source.citation: Clark MA, Douglas M, Choi J (2018). Biology 2e. OpenStax.

claims.value: Set in a single row of about 3,500 cells, the inner hair cells are the primary auditory receptors.
claims.quote: The inner hair cells are the primary auditory receptors and exist in a single row, numbering approximately 3,500.

source.citation: Clark MA, Douglas M, Choi J (2018). Biology 2e. OpenStax.

claims.value: The stereocilia reach up to the overlying tectorial membrane, so when pressure waves from the scala move the basilar membrane, the tectorial membrane slides across them.
claims.quote: The stereocilia extend up from the hair cells to the overlying tectorial membrane, which is attached medially to the organ of Corti. When the pressure waves from the scala move the basilar membrane, the tectorial membrane slides across the stereocilia.

source.citation: Betts JG, Young KA, Wise JA, Johnson E, Poe B, Kruse DH, Korol O, Johnson JE, Womble M, DeSaix P (2022). Anatomy and Physiology 2e. OpenStax.

claims.value: The stereocilia are mechanoreceptors: when vibrations bend them, gated ion channels open, depolarizing the hair cell so a signal passes to the cochlear nerve.
claims.quote: All of the stereocilia are mechanoreceptors, and when bent by vibrations they respond by opening a gated ion channel (refer to ). As a result, the hair cell membrane is depolarized, and a signal is transmitted to the chochlear nerve.

source.citation: Clark MA, Douglas M, Choi J (2018). Biology 2e. OpenStax.

claims.value: Bending the stereocilia toward the tallest one puts tension on the protein tethers between them, opening ion channels that depolarize the cell and trigger impulses in the afferent nerve fibers attached to it.
claims.quote: When the stereocilia bend toward the tallest member of their array, tension in the protein tethers opens ion channels in the hair cell membrane. This will depolarize the hair cell membrane, triggering nerve impulses that travel down the afferent nerve fibers attached to the hair cells.

source.citation: Betts JG, Young KA, Wise JA, Johnson E, Poe B, Kruse DH, Korol O, Johnson JE, Womble M, DeSaix P (2022). Anatomy and Physiology 2e. OpenStax.

claims.value: Bending the stereocilia the other way, toward the shortest one, slackens the tethers and closes the ion channels.
claims.quote: When the stereocilia bend toward the shortest member of their array, the tension on the tethers slackens and the ion channels close.

source.citation: Betts JG, Young KA, Wise JA, Johnson E, Poe B, Kruse DH, Korol O, Johnson JE, Womble M, DeSaix P (2022). Anatomy and Physiology 2e. OpenStax.

claims.value: Even in silence, slight tension on the tethers between the upright stereocilia keeps the hair cell slightly depolarized.
claims.quote: When no sound is present, and the stereocilia are standing straight, a small amount of tension still exists on the tethers, keeping the membrane potential of the hair cell slightly depolarized.

source.citation: Betts JG, Young KA, Wise JA, Johnson E, Poe B, Kruse DH, Korol O, Johnson JE, Womble M, DeSaix P (2022). Anatomy and Physiology 2e. OpenStax.

claims.value: When its hairs bend, the hair cell releases an excitatory neurotransmitter at a synapse with a sensory neuron, which then carries action potentials to the central nervous system.
claims.quote: When the hairs bend, they release an excitatory neurotransmitter at a synapse with a sensory neuron, which then conducts action potentials to the central nervous system.

source.citation: Clark MA, Douglas M, Choi J (2018). Biology 2e. OpenStax.

claims.value: Inner hair cells are the most important route for auditory information to the brain: about 90 percent of the afferent neurons carry their signals, and each cell synapses with about 10 of them.
claims.quote: The inner hair cells are most important for conveying auditory information to the brain. About 90 percent of the afferent neurons carry information from inner hair cells, with each hair cell synapsing with 10 or so neurons.

source.citation: Clark MA, Douglas M, Choi J (2018). Biology 2e. OpenStax.

claims.value: Because the tectorial membrane moves only where the basilar membrane moves, and each region of that membrane moves only at a specific frequency, the hair cells in a region respond only to that frequency.
claims.quote: As stated above, a given region of the basilar membrane will only move if the incoming sound is at a specific frequency. Because the tectorial membrane only moves where the basilar membrane moves, the hair cells in this region will also only respond to sounds of this specific frequency.

source.citation: Betts JG, Young KA, Wise JA, Johnson E, Poe B, Kruse DH, Korol O, Johnson JE, Womble M, DeSaix P (2022). Anatomy and Physiology 2e. OpenStax.

claims.value: Adjacent inner hair cells differ in response frequency by only about 0.2 percent, so neighboring cells respond to slightly different pitches.
claims.quote: The difference in response frequency between adjacent inner hair cells is about 0.2 percent.

source.citation: Clark MA, Douglas M, Choi J (2018). Biology 2e. OpenStax.

claims.value: A hair cell's place along the cochlea sets its pitch: cells at the apex detect frequencies as low as 20 Hz, and cells at the base, near the round and oval windows, encode frequencies around 20 kHz.
claims.quote: Frequencies as low as 20 Hz are detected by hair cells at the apex, or tip, of the cochlea. Frequencies in the higher ranges of 20 KHz are encoded by hair cells at the base of the cochlea, close to the round and oval windows

source.citation: Betts JG, Young KA, Wise JA, Johnson E, Poe B, Kruse DH, Korol O, Johnson JE, Womble M, DeSaix P (2022). Anatomy and Physiology 2e. OpenStax.

tier1.text: A bulbous cell that is medially placed in one row in the organ of Corti. In contrast to the outer hair cells, the inner hair cells are fewer in number, have fewer sensory hairs, and are less differentiated.
